newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila share index ends higher on late buying.
newsitem.headline: Manila share index ends higher on late buying.

text.p: The Manila share index gained 47.72 points, or 1.88 percent, to 2,586.69 points on Thursday, propped up by late session bargain hunting on blue chip issues, traders said.

"The market is up. It's strange but true. It's still because the Fed did not raise rates and all is quiet until the next bad news comes around," said Allan Araullo, vice-president at Regina Capital Development Corp.
"This is just bargain-hunting and we will likely meet resistance at 2,630. What we need is volume," said Jonathan Ravelas, head of sales at Asian Capital Equities.
Turnover was a modest at 2.01 billion pesos though higher than the previous day's 1.52 billion.
All indices rose. Gainers outpaced losers 89 to 28 with 64 unchanged issues.
Blue chips that buoyed up the index in late session were Ayala Land Inc, Metrobank MBT PS Meralco B and the Philippine National Bank.
C&P Homes Inc, however, notably bucked the trend as it hit a record low close of 8.50 pesos still on leftover negative sentiment due to recent fears of a property crash, traders said.
Teresa Lee, vice-president at Asiamerit Securities said sentiment improved after a two percentage-point cut in overnight rates by the Central bank.
But some traders said fund managers are still adopting a wait-and-see attitude not just on the Philipines but on the region.
Ravelas said he expects the market to move sideways on Friday and that any rallies would be met by selling.
